const r1 = await tools.progress.append_progress({content: `STAGE: candidate selection and scope check (ideation_3, round_langgraph_trial_20261104)
GOAL: pick one coupling position not covered by the three rejected earlier rounds.
READ: the round brief's rejected list (poincare-frechet-successor-codebook = curved successor-Frechet CODEBOOK UPDATE; CURVCTRL-SID = per-LEVEL curvature from prefix transition score; BRad-RQ = behaviour-ranked RADIAL assignment; plus LORENTZ-SUCCPROFILE-SMOOTH-RQ, behcone-prefix-rq, succboost-geoshift).
OBSERVED: all three rejected rounds act on (a) codebook centroid movement, (b) per-level curvature scalar, (c) radial ranking of the assignment. None acts on the CHART in which the residual is expressed, i.e. on the basepoint of the exp/log map that carries the residual from level l to level l+1.
REASONING: choose a different degree of freedom: keep the codebook shared and unmoved, keep curvature fixed at c=1, and instead move the exponential chart of the residual to a behaviour-derived successor basepoint of the current PREFIX bucket, with a constant-free geodesic blend weight = quantisation-error / (error + behaviour gap). Removing behaviour collapses the blend to 0 (standard hyperbolic RQ); removing curvature collapses exp/log/Frechet to linear/Euclidean. Coupling is a single equation, so no standalone loss is needed.
STILL OPEN: none for the write-up; the mechanism is fully specified and constant-free.`});
const r2 = await tools.progress.append_progress({content: `STAGE: final answer (ideation_3)
STATUS: one distinct, implementable, in-scope idea; no training run performed (per round policy).

IDEA: SUCC-CHART-RQ
TITLE: Successor-anchored exponential chart: the RQ residual at every level is geodesically re-expressed at a behaviour-derived prefix-successor basepoint
MOTIVATION: A generative recommender consumes SID prefixes as tokens, so what matters is that an early prefix already narrows the plausible NEXT item. A plain residual quantiser spends levels 2..L on the reconstruction error of the item's own embedding, which is behaviour-blind: two items in the same prefix bucket but with disjoint successor sets keep diverging down branches that carry no transition information. The residual chart, not the codebook, is the untapped degree of freedom.
NOVELTY: Earlier rounds moved the codebook centroids (Poincare-Frechet successor codebook), the per-level curvature scalar (CURVCTRL-SID) or the radial rank of the assignment (BRad-RQ). SUCC-CHART-RQ leaves the codebook shared and static in position and leaves curvature fixed at c=1; it changes the POINT AT WHICH THE RESIDUAL IS EXPRESSED (the basepoint of exp/log), selected per item and per level from the successor distribution of that item's current PREFIX BUCKET, and it transports the residual along the geodesic with a weight that is the error-to-signal ratio, so no coupling hyperparameter exists to tune.
CHANGE: After each level's code is chosen, the residual is not passed on verbatim; it is replaced by the point on the Poincare geodesic from the chosen code to a successor-Frechet basepoint of the item's prefix bucket, blended by error/(error+behaviour gap), and that point is what level l+1 quantises.
SPECIFICATION: see equations below. Behaviour: directed within-session item transitions of the training split give p(j|i); the level-(l+1) basepoint b_{l+1,i} is the weighted Poincare Frechet mean (Karcher iteration) of the ball-mapped encoder outputs of the top-M successors of the prefix bucket containing i. Geometry: fixed curvature c=1 Poincare ball, Mobius addition, exp/log maps at the chosen code, geodesic interpolation, hyperbolic reconstruction distance. Coupling: x_{l+1} = exp_{c_l}( (1-a_l) log_{c_l}(x_l) + a_l log_{c_l}(b_{l+1,i}) ), a_l = d_P(x_l,c_l)/(d_P(x_l,c_l)+d_P(c_l,b_{l+1,i})+eps). Switches B, G exist in code; only both-on is trained.
COST: per step (batch 1023, L=4, d=64): 4 x 1023 pairs of exp/log plus 4 x 1023 Mobius sums, about 12k curved ops, under 1 ms on one card: <5% over baseline step time. Per epoch (24 steps, 24556 items): prefix-bucket hashing 24556 x 4 keys (~0.1 s CPU/GPU) and basepoint refresh 24556 x 5 (levels) x M=16 neighbours x 5 Karcher iterations x d=64, about 5e8 flops (~0.05 s). Over 3000 epochs the refresh is the only added recurring cost, roughly 1.5e12 flops total, i.e. minutes, done on the same four cards with stop-gradient.
HYPOTHESIS: If the successor basepoint is a genuinely useful conditioning signal, then levels 2..4 will stop encoding pure reconstruction error and start encoding which successor branch the item belongs to: the diagnostic P(next item's level-l code | first l codes) must rise at l=2..4 versus a plain hyperbolic RQ, and the Stage 3 test recall@10 must exceed 0.065 in the single both-on run. If prefix predictability rises but recall does not, the generative model is not exploiting the reallocated bits and the idea should be dropped.
RISKS: (1) The behaviour pull corrupts the reconstruction objective, so reconstruction quality drops enough that the decoder cannot identify the item, netting out negative. (2) Prefix buckets are coarse and noisy early in training, so the basepoint is meaningless for the first few hundred epochs; the refresh schedule may need a warm start at the origin, which is a mechanism choice that must be fixed a priori, not tuned. (3) Long-tail items have no successors, so their basepoint falls back to the origin and they receive no benefit. (4) Poincare arithmetic near the boundary can produce NaNs under mixed precision. (5) Single-run seed noise can swamp a 0.001-0.003 recall effect.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Directed within-session item transitions (successor distribution p(j|i)), aggregated to the SID prefix level.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: From the training split only: for every training session, every consecutive pair (u_t, u_{t+1}) increments n(u_t,u_{t+1}); p(j|i)=n(i,j)/sum_j n(i,j) after dropping self-pairs. For level l+1 and item i, q_{l+1}(j|i) = (1/|G_l(i)|) sum_{i' in G_l(i)} p(j|i'), where G_l(i) is the set of training items sharing the first l codes with i (G_0(i)={i}); the basepoint uses the top-M=16 entries of q.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: p is estimated only from consecutive pairs inside training-split sessions; validation and test sessions never touch n(.,.), never define G_l, never define a basepoint. Prefix buckets are formed from the model's own codebook assignment of TRAINING items only. Nothing about a validation or test item enters the codebook, the basepoints, the SID of a training item, or any gradient.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Poincare ball of fixed curvature c=1 (sectional curvature -1), with Mobius addition a (+) b, exp_x(v)= x (+)( tanh(sqrt(c)||v||/2) v/(sqrt(c)||v||) ), log_x(y)= (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c)||(-x)(+)y||) ((-x)(+)y)/||(-x)(+)y||, d_P(x,y)=(2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c)||(-x)(+)y||); the basepoint Frechet mean is the Karcher fixed point m <- exp_m( sum_j w_j log_m(z_j) ).
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: Inside the residual-quantiser recurrence of the RQ-VAE at every level l=1..L (L=4), and inside the reconstruction loss d_P(z, MobiusSum(c_1..c_L))^2; also inside the basepoint computation (Frechet mean) that is refreshed every epoch with stop-gradient.
COUPLING PATH: behaviour -> q_{l+1}(.|i) -> TopM -> weighted Karcher mean b_{l+1,i} in the ball -> log_{c_l}(b_{l+1,i}) inside the geodesic blend -> transported residual x_{l+1} -> code choice k_{l+1} -> SID prefix -> Stage 3 tokens. One chain, no side losses; setting the behaviour term to zero sets a_l=0 and the chain degenerates to standard hyperbolic RQ; replacing the curved ops with Euclidean ones degenerates to a linear residual blend.
COUPLING EQUATION: x_{l+1,i} = exp_{c_{l}}( (1-a_{l,i}) log_{c_l}(x_{l,i}) + a_{l,i} log_{c_l}( b_{l+1,i}(q) ) ), with a_{l,i} = d_P(x_{l,i}, c_{l}) / ( d_P(x_{l,i}, c_{l}) + d_P(c_{l}, b_{l+1,i}(q)) + eps ), and b_{l+1,i}(q) = argmin_m sum_j q_{l+1}(j|i) d_P^2(m, z_j).
OBSERVABLES: (i) the prefix-successor diagnostic P(level-(l+1) code of the true next item | first l codes), l=1..3, must rise; (ii) codebook usage at levels 2..4 must shift toward successor-discriminative directions (measured by the entropy of q within each code); (iii) mean hyperbolic reconstruction error must stay within a small factor of the plain RQ; (iv) Stage 3 test_recall@10 > 0.065.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: a_l := 0 for all l (b unused, q never read), so x_{l+1} = x_l and every level quantises the standard hyperbolic residual; basepoints are still computed for logging but never enter the computation.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: exp/log/Mobius/d_P replaced by their Euclidean counterparts, i.e. b is the arithmetic weighted mean of z_j, distances are L2, and the blend is the linear interpolation c + (1-a)(x-c) + a(b-c); behaviour still enters through b and a.
ABLATION BOTH ON: the full coupled run above, the only arm actually trained.
SPEC EQUATIONS: c=1, delta=1e-3.
ball(v) = tanh(||v||) v/||v||, with ||v|| clamped to [1e-8, 0.999].
Mobius: x (+) y = ((1+2c<x,y>+c||y||^2) x + (1-c||x||^2) y) / (1+2c<x,y>+c^2||x||^2||y||^2).
log/exp as in HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR.
Epoch refresh (stop-grad): z_i = ball(enc(i)); for l=1..L, G_l(i)= items sharing first l codes; q_{l+1}(j|i)=mean over G_l(i) of p(j|.); S=TopM(q); b_{l+1,i}=Karcher(z_S, q(S)/sum q(S)).
Step: for l=1..L: k_l=argmin_k d_P(x_l, C[l,k]); c=C[l,k_l]; g=d_P(c, b_{l+1,i}); e=d_P(x_l, c); a=e/(e+g+eps) if g>1e-6 else 0; a=clamp(a,0,1); x_{l+1}=exp_c((1-a)log_c(x_l)+a log_c(b_{l+1,i})).
Loss: L = mean_i d_P(z_i, MobiusSum_{l}(C[l,k_{l,i}]))^2 + 0.25 * mean_i sum_l d_P(x_{l,i}, C[l,k_{l,i}])^2 (the second weight is the baseline's documented default, unchanged and untuned).
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: encoder outputs z_i (batch, d), codebooks C[1..L] (K, d) in the ball, successor table p (sparse), current prefix buckets, curvature c=1. Outputs: per item the code tuple (k_1..k_L) that is the SID, plus the transported residuals x_2..x_{L+1} used for the next level's assignment and the loss terms.
SAFEGUARDS: clamp ||z||, ||x|| and ||c|| to <= 0.999 before artanh; compute artanh via torch.atanh on a value clamped to 1-1e-6; add eps=1e-7 in every Mobius denominator; set a=0 when g<1e-6 or when q is empty (no successors -> b=0); fall back to basepoint 0 for items whose prefix bucket has zero transition mass; stop-gradient on b and on the bucket assignment; keep the codebook initialised with radius <= 0.5 so no code starts near the boundary; codebook and residual tensors in float32 even under AMP; assert finite loss every 100 steps.
END IDEA`});
return [r1, r2];

COUPLING EQUATION: x_{l+1,i} = exp_{c_{l}}( (1-a_{l,i}) log_{c_l}(x_{l,i}) + a_{l,i} log_{c_l}( b_{l+1,i}(q) ) ), with a_{l,i} = d_P(x_{l,i}, c_{l}) / ( d_P(x_{l,i}, c_{l}) + d_P(c_{l}, b_{l+1,i}(q)) + eps ), and b_{l+1,i}(q) = argmin_m sum_j q_{l+1}(j|i) d_P^2(m, z_j).

IDEA: SUCC-CHART-RQ
TITLE: Successor-anchored exponential chart: every RQ residual is geodesically re-expressed at a behaviour-derived prefix-successor basepoint
MOTIVATION: A generative recommender consumes SID prefixes as tokens, so what matters is that an early prefix already narrows the plausible NEXT item. A plain residual quantiser spends levels 2..L on the reconstruction error of the item's own embedding, which is behaviour-blind: two items in the same prefix bucket with disjoint successor sets keep diverging down branches that carry no transition information.
NOVELTY: The earlier rounds moved the codebook centroids (Poincare-Frechet successor codebook), the per-level curvature scalar (CURVCTRL-SID), or the radial rank of the assignment (BRad-RQ). SUCC-CHART-RQ keeps the codebook shared and unmoved and keeps curvature fixed at c=1; it changes the POINT AT WHICH THE RESIDUAL IS EXPRESSED (basepoint of exp/log), chosen per item and per level from the successor distribution of that item's current PREFIX bucket, and it transports the residual along a geodesic with a weight equal to the error-to-signal ratio, so there is no coupling hyperparameter to tune.
CHANGE: After each level's code is chosen, the residual is replaced by the point on the Poincare geodesic running from that code to a successor-Frechet basepoint of the item's prefix bucket, blended by error/(error+behaviour gap), and that point is what level l+1 quantises.

The level-(l+1) basepoint b_{l+1,i} is the weighted Poincare (Karcher) Frechet mean of the ball-mapped encoder outputs of the top-M=16 successors of the level-l prefix bucket of i. Geometry: fixed curvature c=1 Poincare ball, Mobius addition, exp/log at the chosen code, geodesic interpolation, hyperbolic reconstruction distance. Switches B (behaviour off) and G (geometry off) exist in code; only both-on is trained.
COST: Per step (batch 1023, L=4, d=64): 4x1023 exp/log pairs plus 4x1023 Mobius sums ~12k curved ops, under 1 ms on one card, under 5% of baseline step time.
